---
kind: mdbase.contract
contract_type: record
id: mdbase.daily-note
version: 1.0.0
name: Daily note
description: One record per local calendar day, identified by its date.
record_schema:
  dialect: json-schema-2020-12
  ref: ../../schemas/mdbase.daily-note/1.0.0.schema.json
---

# Daily note

A record exposed through `mdbase.daily-note` represents one local calendar day.
`date` is an RFC 3339 full-date such as `2026-10-30`: a civil day with no time
and no time zone. It names the day the user lived, not an instant, so it does
not change when the user or the collection changes time zone.

## Identity

A daily note is identified by its `date` value, never by its path or file name.
An implementing type may store the date in the path, for example with
`collection.path.fields`, but consumers read the contract field and never parse
paths or file names themselves.

## Discovery

Implementing this contract is how a collection declares which of its records
are daily notes. An application discovers daily notes through this contract's
type implementations, not through a folder, a file-name format, or a reserved
type name, path, or frontmatter value.

## One record per day

A collection should hold at most one record per date across all types that
implement this contract. To find the note for a day, an application queries
every implementing type for that date:

- No record: the day has no daily note. This is not an error.
- Exactly one record: that record is the day's note.
- Several records: the date is ambiguous. Applications MUST report the
  ambiguity and MUST NOT silently pick one of the records, merge them, or
  write to one of them as the day's note.

A partial or failed query cannot establish that a day has no note or exactly
one note. Implementing types may declare `collection.unique` on their date
field so the engine reports duplicates within the type.

## Creating a daily note

An application creates a daily note through the implementing type's ordinary
create operation and path policy. File names, folders, templates and the body
belong to the type and the collection; the contract does not prescribe them.
An application that opens the note for a day, such as today in the user's
time zone, first looks for an existing record for that date and creates one
only when there is none.

## Other day data

Other applications may attach their own data to a day, such as time blocks or
completed pomodoros, through separate contracts implemented by the same type.
This contract defines only the day itself.

This artifact is passive. Implementing it grants no authority to read, create,
or modify any record.

---
kind: mdbase.type
name: daily-note
version: 1
description: One note per calendar day, named by its date in the Daily folder.
match:
  path_glob: 'Daily/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9].md'
schema:
  dialect: json-schema-2020-12
  value:
    $schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
    title: Daily note
    description: One local calendar day represented by an ordinary note. The date is stored in the file name, not in frontmatter.
    type: object
    required:
      - date
    properties:
      date:
        type: string
        format: date
        description: The day this note is for, as a full calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, with no time or time zone. It is stored in the file name (Daily/2026-10-30.md), so changing it renames the note; do not also write it in frontmatter.
    additionalProperties: true
collection:
  path:
    pattern: 'Daily/{date}.md'
    fields:
      - date
  unique:
    - field: date
      scope: type
  display:
    name_field: date
    icon: calendar
implements:
  - contract: mdbase.daily-note
    version: 1.0.0
    fields:
      date: date
---

# Daily note

One note per day, at `Daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. The date lives only in the file
name: apps read it from the path, and creating a note for a date puts it at
that date's path. The rest of the note is yours: write in the body and add any
frontmatter fields you like.

```text
Daily/2026-10-30.md
```

Only files in `Daily/` whose name is a date belong to this type, so other notes
in the folder are left alone. A collection should have one note per date; two
notes with the same date are reported, and apps treat that day as ambiguous
rather than choosing one.

## Use an existing daily-notes folder

To adopt notes another tool already writes, such as Obsidian's daily notes,
change the folder in both `match.path_glob` and `collection.path.pattern`. For
notes in `Journal/`:

```yaml
match:
  path_glob: 'Journal/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9].md'
collection:
  path:
    pattern: 'Journal/{date}.md'
    fields: [date]
```

Notes are recognised by their path, so existing files need no frontmatter
changes. File names must use the `YYYY-MM-DD` form.

This type belongs to your collection once installed. Apps find daily notes
through the `mdbase.daily-note` contract, not through this folder or file name,
so you can move them, or add other types that implement the contract, as long
as each date has one note.
